c: The rest of the words of Baruch, which were not hidden, from the time when the people were taken captive to Babylon.

When the king of the Chaldeans was about to take the children of Israel captive, God spoke to Jeremiah and said to him: Jeremiah, my chosen one, rise and go out of this city, you and Baruch, for I am about to destroy it because of the many sins of those who live in it.
For your prayer is like a strong pillar in the midst of the city, and like a wall of adamant around it. So now rise and go out, before the army of the Chaldeans comes and surrounds the city.
And Jeremiah answered, saying: I beseech you, my Lord, allow your servant to speak before you. And the Lord said to him: Speak, my chosen one, Jeremiah.

And Jeremiah spoke and said: Lord, you who hold all things, will you hand over this chosen city into the hands of the Chaldeans, so that the king and his people may boast and say, We have overpowered the city of God?
No, Lord. If it is your will, let it be destroyed by your own hand.
And the Lord said to Jeremiah: Since you are my chosen one, rise and go out, you and Baruch, for I am about to destroy it because of the sins of those who live in it.
Neither the king nor his army could enter the city unless I first opened its gates.

Rise now and go to Baruch and tell him these words. And when you have risen, at the sixth hour of the night, come to the wall of the city, and I will show you that unless I first destroy the city, they cannot enter it.
And when he had said this, the Lord departed from Jeremiah.
Then Jeremiah tore his garments, put ashes on his head, and went into the temple.
When Baruch saw Jeremiah with dust on his head and his garments torn, he cried out with a loud voice, saying: Father Jeremiah, what has happened to you? What sin have the people committed?
For whenever the people sinned, Jeremiah would grieve, put ashes on his head, and pray for the people until their guilt was forgiven them.
And Baruch asked him, saying: Father Jeremiah, what has happened to you, and what has happened to the people?

Jeremiah said to him: Take care that we do not tear our garments, but tear our hearts; and let us not draw water into the troughs, but weep until we fill them with tears, for from now on there will be no mercy for this people.

And Baruch said: Father Jeremiah, what has happened to you? And Jeremiah said to him: God is handing the city over into the hand of the king of the Chaldeans, and he will take the people captive in evil.
When Baruch heard all this, he tore his garments and said: Father Jeremiah, who sent you this word?
Jeremiah said to him: Wait with me until the sixth hour of the night, so that you may know that the word is true.
And they stayed in the temple, weeping.
When the sixth hour of the night came, as the Lord had told Jeremiah, he went out with Baruch, and they came to the wall of the city and sat there waiting.
And there was the sound of a trumpet, and angels came out of heaven carrying torches of fire in their hands, and they stood on the wall of the city.
Then Jeremiah and Baruch wept, saying: Now we know that the word is true.
And Jeremiah begged the angels, saying: I beseech you all, do not destroy the city until I ask the Lord one thing.
And the Lord spoke to the angels, saying: Do not destroy the city until I have spoken with Jeremiah, my chosen one.
Then Jeremiah spoke, saying: I beseech you, my Lord, command me to speak with you. And he said to him: Say what you wish, my chosen one, Jeremiah.

And Jeremiah said to him: Now we know, my Lord, that you are handing the city over into the hand of its enemies, and the people of Babylon will take it. What do you want me to do with the holy vessels of the service with which we serve in secret? And what do you want me to do with them?

And the Lord said to him: Take them and hand them over to the earth and to the temple, saying: And you, earth, hear the voice of your Creator, who made you in the power of the waters and sealed you with seven seals. Receive your adornment, and keep the vessels of your service until the coming of the Beloved.

And Jeremiah spoke and said: I beseech you, my Lord, show me what I should do for Abimelech the Ethiopian, who did much to keep the people, and your servant Jeremiah more than all the people of the city. It was he who brought me up out of the pit of mire, and I do not want him to see the ruin and destruction of the city, so that he may not grieve.
And the Lord said to Jeremiah: Send him to the vineyard of Agrippa, by the mountain road, and I will shelter him until I bring the people back to the city.
And you, Jeremiah, go with the people until you reach the land of Babylon, and stay there and prophesy to them until I bring them back to their city. But leave Baruch there in Jerusalem.
When the Lord had told Jeremiah all this, he departed from Jeremiah into heaven.

Then Jeremiah and Baruch went into the temple and handed over all the vessels of the service to the earth, as the Lord had commanded them, and at once the earth swallowed them up. And the two of them sat down and wept.

Early the next morning Jeremiah sent Abimelech away, saying: Take a basket and go by the mountain road to the vineyard of Agrippa, and bring a few figs for the sick among the people, for the joy of the Lord and his glory are upon your head. And he went, as he had commanded him.
Early the next morning the army of the Chaldeans surrounded the city, and the great angel blew the trumpet and said: Enter, army of the Chaldeans; behold, the gates are opened for you.
Then the king entered with his army, and they took all the people captive.

And Jeremiah took the keys of the temple, went outside the city, and threw these keys before the sun, saying: To you I say, O sun: take the keys of the house of God and keep them until the day when the Lord asks you for them.
For we were not found worthy to keep them; we were found wanting because of our sins.
And while Jeremiah was weeping for the people, they led him out, driving him along, and took him with the people to Babylon.

But Baruch took ashes, put them on his head, sat down, and lamented with this lament, saying: Why has Jerusalem been laid waste? It is because of the sins of the beloved people that she was given into the hand of her enemy; because of our sins and the sins of the people.
But let the sinners not boast and say: We were strong enough to take the city of God by our power. It was not by your strength that you overcame her; she was given to you because of our sins.
And our God will have mercy on us and bring us back to our city, but for you there is no life.
Blessed are our fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, for they went out of this world and did not see the destruction of this city.
When he had said this, he went out weeping and said: I grieve for you, Jerusalem. And he went out of the city and lived in a tomb, and angels would come and tell him about all things.

And Abimelech brought the figs at noon, from where Jeremiah had sent him. He found a shady tree, sat down in its shade to rest a little, leaned his head on the basket of figs, and fell asleep. He slept for sixty-six years and did not wake from his sleep.
After those days he rose and woke from his sleep, and said: I have slept only a little, for my head is still heavy and I have not had enough sleep.
He uncovered the basket of figs and found the figs fresh, with their milk still dripping.

He wanted to sleep again, because his head was heavy and he had not had enough sleep, but he said: I am afraid to sleep and be late, so that my father Jeremiah may not scold me, for he sent me in haste in the morning. Now I will rise and go, for the heat is burning, and there is no rest anywhere.

So he rose, took his basket of figs, and went into the city of Jerusalem. But he did not recognize the city, nor his own house, and he said: Blessed are you, Lord, for a great bewilderment has come upon me.

And he said: Is this not the city of Jerusalem? Perhaps I have lost my way, because I came by the mountain road. Or else it is because my head is heavy and I have not had enough sleep, and my mind is confused. How shall I tell Jeremiah this, how the city has become strange to me?
He looked for every landmark in the city, to know whether it was Jerusalem. He went back into the city again and looked for someone who knew him, and found no one.
And he said: Blessed are you, Lord, for a great bewilderment has fallen upon me. And he went far out of the city again and sat down, grieving, not knowing where to go.
He set down the basket of figs and said: I will sit here until God takes this confusion away from me.
After he had sat there, he saw an old man coming from the field, and Abimelech said to him: I say to you, old man, what is this city? And the old man said to him: It is Jerusalem.
Abimelech said to him: Where is Jeremiah the priest, and Baruch the Levite, and all the people of this city? For I have found no one.

The old man said to him: Are you not from this city? And only now, after all the time you have lived, do you remember Jeremiah, to ask about him? Jeremiah is in Babylon with the people, for he was taken captive and handed over to Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Persia, and he went there to prophesy to them.

When Abimelech heard this from the old man, he said to him: If you were not an old man, I would have insulted you and laughed at you. But it is not right for people to despise an old man. If you were not old, I would have said that you are out of your mind.

As for what you say, that the people have been taken captive to Babylon: even if the floodgates of heaven had come down on them, there would not have been time for them to go to Babylon. And yet you say they have been taken captive to Babylon.

I myself went, as my father Jeremiah sent me, to the vineyard of Agrippa, for a few figs to give to the sick among the people. I went and arrived there, took what he had told me, and turned back. On the way I found a tree and sat under it to rest in the shade, because it was noon. There I leaned on the basket of figs and fell asleep, and when I woke I thought I was late.

I uncovered this basket of figs and found them dripping with milk, just as I had picked them, my friend. And yet you say the people have been taken captive to Babylon. Look, and see that the figs have not withered.
And he uncovered the basket of figs for him and showed it to him. The old man looked and saw that the figs were fresh and their milk was dripping.

Then the old man marvelled and said to Abimelech: You are a righteous man, my son, for God did not want to show you the ruin of the city. God brought rest upon you and kept you alive. Behold, today it is sixty-six years since the people were taken captive to Babylon.
And if you want to know and be sure, my son, look at the fields and see that their crops have barely sprouted, and see that it is not the season for figs.

And Abimelech understood that it was not the time for any of this. Then he said with a loud voice: I bless you, Lord my God, God of heaven and earth, the rest of the souls of the righteous in every place.
And he said to the old man: What month is this? And he said to him: The twelfth day of the month of Nisan, which is Miyazya.
After this Abimelech gave the old man some of the figs, and said to him: May God guide you to the city above, Jerusalem.
Then Abimelech rose and went out of the city and prayed to God, and behold, an angel came and led him to Baruch, and he found him sitting in the tomb.

When they had greeted one another, wept together and embraced, Baruch saw the figs in the basket, lifted his eyes to heaven, and prayed, saying: Great is God, who gives their reward to his righteous ones.
Prepare yourself, my soul, and rejoice, saying to the body of flesh, your holy house: your sorrow will be turned into light. After this the Faithful One will come and bring you back into your body.

Look to your own pure faith, and believe that you will live. Look at these figs: behold, it is sixty-six years since they were picked, and they have not decayed or gone bad, but their milk is dripping until now.
So it will be done to you, my flesh, for you have kept your commandment from the angel of righteousness. He who kept the basket of figs will keep you again by his power.
When Baruch had said this, he said to Abimelech: Rise, let us pray again, so that the Lord may show us the words we should write to Jeremiah in Babylon, about the shelter with which he sheltered you.
And Baruch prayed and said: My strength is God the Lord, and the light that comes from his mouth. I beseech you and bow down to your goodness. Great is your name, and no one can understand it.
Hear the prayer of your servant, so that your will may become clear in my heart, to do it and to send word to your priest Jeremiah in Babylon.

While he was praying this, an angel came and said to him: Baruch, counsellor of the light, do not worry about how you will send word to Jeremiah. Tomorrow, at the hour of light, an eagle will come to you.

And you yourself take care of Jeremiah: write in a letter and say to the children of Israel: Whoever is a stranger among you shall be set apart, for fifteen days, and after this I will bring you into the city, says the Lord.
Whoever is not separated from Babylon within fifteen days, Jeremiah shall go into the city and rebuke them with the people of Babylon, says the Lord.
When the angel had said this, he departed from Baruch. And Baruch sent to the marketplace and brought papyrus and ink, and wrote, saying:
Baruch, the servant of God, writes a letter to Jeremiah in the captivity of Babylon: joy and gladness! For God has not let us go out of this body in sorrow over our disgrace and ruin.
Because of this the Lord has had mercy on our tears and has remembered the covenant he made long ago with our fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
And he sent his angel to me and told me these words, which I send to you. These are the words that the Lord, the God of Israel, spoke, who brought us out of the land of Egypt, out of the fire:

Because you did not keep all his righteous laws, but lifted up your pride and hardened your neck before him, he handed you over to the furnace of Babylon; because you did not listen to my voice, says the Lord, from the mouth of Jeremiah his servant.
Those who have listened I will bring out of Babylon, and they will no longer be strangers from Jerusalem living in Babylon.
And if you want to know them and to tell them apart, test them by the water of the Jordan, and whoever does not listen will be known by this sign, which is greater than a seal.
Having written this, Baruch rose and went out of the tomb.
And the eagle said to him: Greetings, Baruch, steward of the faith.
Baruch said to him: You who speak are chosen among all the birds of heaven; you are known by the brightness of your eyes. Now show me what you are doing here.
The eagle said to him: I was sent here so that you may send me with whatever word you wish.
Baruch said to him: Can you carry these words to Jeremiah in Babylon? And the eagle said to him: That is why I was sent.
And Baruch took the letter, and fifteen figs from the basket of figs that Abimelech had brought, and tied them to the eagle's neck.
And he said to him: To you I say, eagle, king of all the birds: go in peace and in life, and bring news back to us.
Do not be like the raven which Noah sent out and which refused to come back to him, but be like the dove which the third time brought word back to Noah.
So you too, take these good words to Jeremiah and to those of Israel who are with him, that it may go well with you; and take this joy to the people, the chosen of God.

Even if all the birds surround you, and all the enemies of righteousness, wanting to kill you, fight on, and the Lord will give you strength. Do not turn to the right or to the left, but go like an arrow that flies straight, in the power of God.

When Baruch had said this, the eagle flew off with the letter and went to Babylon. It rested on a pillar outside the city, in a deserted place, and waited there until Jeremiah and other people came by.
They were coming that way to bury a man who had died, for Jeremiah had asked Nebuchadnezzar: Give me a piece of land where I may bury those of my people who die. And he gave it to him.

As they were going along, weeping over the dead man, they came in front of the eagle. And the eagle cried out with a loud voice and said: To you I say, Jeremiah, chosen one of God: go and gather all the people, and let them come here to hear the good news I have brought.
When he heard this, he praised God, and at once he gathered all the people, with their wives and children, and they came to where the eagle was.
Then the eagle came down onto the dead body and touched it, and it came back to life. He did this so that they might believe. And all the people marvelled at what had happened.
And they said: Perhaps this is the God who appeared to our fathers in the wilderness with Moses, and who has taken the form of an eagle and appeared to us as a great eagle.
And the eagle said to Jeremiah: Come, take this letter and read it to the people. And he read it to them.
When the people heard it, they all wept together, put ashes on their heads, and said to Jeremiah: Save us! What must we do to return to our city?
Jeremiah rose and said to them: Do everything you have heard in the letter, and he will bring you back to your city.
And Jeremiah wrote a letter to Baruch, saying: My beloved son, do not grow weary in prayer, beseeching God for us, that he may guide us on our way until we go out by the command of this sinful king.
You have found righteousness before God, who did not let you come with us, so that you would not see the evil that is done to the people in Babylon.

It is as when a father has an only son, and the son is handed over to be punished: those who are with the father to comfort him cover his face, so that he may not see his son and waste away with grief. In the same way God has had mercy on you, and did not let you come to Babylon, so that you would not see the affliction of the people.

For since we came to this city we have not had rest from grief until today; today it is sixty-six years. We go out and find some of our people hanged by King Nebuchadnezzar, weeping and saying: Have mercy on us, god Sor.

When I heard these words, I grieved and wept, because they were calling on another god, as they hung there, and saying: Have mercy on us. And again I remember the feasts we kept in Jerusalem before we were taken captive, and as I remember them I go back into my house in pain and weep.
So now, beseech our God where you are, you and Abimelech, for the people, that they may listen to my voice and the words of my mouth, so that they may come out of Persia.

And now I tell you: all the days we have lived here they have pressed us, saying: Sing us a new song from the songs of Zion, the song of your God. And we say to them: How can we sing for you, while we are in a foreign land?
When Jeremiah had written this, he tied his letter to the eagle's neck and said to it: Go in peace, and may the Lord watch over you.
And the eagle went and flew off and brought the letter to Baruch. Baruch took it and read the letter, and he wept when he heard of the sufferings and afflictions of the people.
But Jeremiah took the figs and gave them to the sick among the people, and he remained, teaching them not to do the works of the people of Babylon.

When the day came on which God would bring the people out of Babylon, the Lord said to Jeremiah: Rise, you and your people, and come to the Jordan, and say to the people: The Lord wills that the works of the people of Babylon be put away.

As for the men among you who have married wives from them, and the women who have married men from them, let us test them. Those who listen to you I will bring back to Jerusalem; but those who do not listen to you, do not let them enter it.
So Jeremiah read all this to them, and brought them to the Jordan to test them.

While he was telling them the words the Lord had spoken to him, those who had married wavered and would not listen to Jeremiah. Some said to him: We will never leave our wives; we will take them with us to our city. And they crossed the Jordan and came to Jerusalem.
Jeremiah, Baruch and Abimelech stood there, saying: No man who has married a wife from Babylon shall enter our city.
And those who had married wives said to one another: Come, let us go back to Babylon. And they went back.

But when the people of Babylon saw them, they came out to keep them from coming in, and would not let them enter Babylon, saying: You hated us before, and you left us in secret. Because of this you shall not enter our city, for we have sworn by the name of our god not to receive you or your daughters, since you went away from us in secret.
When they heard this, they turned back toward Jerusalem and built themselves towns around Jerusalem, and they called that town Samaria.
And Jeremiah sent to them, saying: Repent, and behold, the angel of righteousness will come and bring you back to your high place.
They remained there rejoicing, and offered sacrifice for the people for seven days. On the tenth day after this, Jeremiah offered a sacrifice alone.
And Jeremiah prayed, saying: Holy, holy, holy, sweet fragrance to men, and true light that shines on me until I come before you.

I beseech you for your people. I ask you by the honey-sweet voice of the seraphim, and by the fragrance of the incense of the cherubim. I ask you, yes, by Michael who sings your praise, the angel of righteousness, who opens the gates of righteousness until they enter in.
I beseech you, Lord of all, Lord who holds all things and made all things, the seen and the unborn, who brought all things to completion, with whom all creation was hidden before it was made.
When he had prayed this and finished his prayer, Jeremiah was standing in the temple, and with him Baruch and Abimelech, and Jeremiah became like a man whose soul has left him.
At once Baruch and Abimelech fell down and cried out with a loud voice, saying: Woe to us! Our father Jeremiah, the priest of God, has gone from us.
When the people heard this, they ran to him and found Jeremiah fallen and dead. They wept, tore their garments, put ashes on their heads, and wept bitterly.
After they had made ready to bury him, a voice came, saying: Do not wrap him for burial. He is alive, and his soul will come back into his body again.
When they heard this voice, they did not wrap him, but stayed around him, keeping watch for three days, until his soul came back into his body.

And a voice came in the midst of them all, saying: Praise with one voice, praise God, and all of you praise the Messiah, the Son of God, who awakens you and judges you: Jesus, the Son of God, the light of all the world, the lamp that does not go out, and the life of faith.
After these days there will be three hundred and three weeks of days until his coming upon the earth.

The tree of life which is in paradise, which no one planted, will make all the trees, those that bear fruit and those that are dry, come to him. He will make them bear fruit and sprout, and their fruit will dwell with the angels.

And as for the trees that are planted, that they may flourish and lift their tops high toward the sky, he will see to it that their roots do not wither, like a plant whose root has not taken hold in the earth.

What is red as crimson they will make white as wool; sweet water will become bitter, and the bitter will become sweet, in great gladness; and the joys of God will come to the islands, so that they bear fruit through the word of the mouth of his Son.

He himself will come into the world and choose for himself twelve apostles, so that they may see what I have seen: the glorious One sent from his Father, who comes into the world, and goes up on the Mount of Olives, and fills the hungry soul.
In this way Jeremiah spoke of the Son of God, that he would come into the world.

When the people heard this, they were angry about it and said: These are the words of Isaiah son of Amoz, who said: I have seen God, the Son of God. Come, let us do to him as we did to Isaiah. But half of them said: No, let us stone him with stones.
Baruch and Abimelech cried out to them, saying: Do not kill him with this death.
And Baruch and Abimelech grieved for Jeremiah, for they had not yet let him tell them the hidden things he had seen.
And Jeremiah said to them: Be still, do not weep, for they cannot kill me until I have told you everything I have seen. Now bring me a stone.
They brought him a stone, and he set it up and said: Eternal light, make this stone take the appearance of a man. At once the stone took on the appearance of Jeremiah and looked like him.
And they began to stone the stone, thinking that it was Jeremiah.
And Jeremiah told Baruch and Abimelech all the hidden things he had seen. After he had finished telling them, he went and stood in the midst of the people, wishing to complete his service.
Then the stone cried out to them and said: O foolish children of Israel, why do you stone me, thinking that I am Jeremiah? Behold, Jeremiah is standing in your midst.
When they saw him, they ran at him with many stones and put an end to his life. They buried him, took that stone and set it on his grave like a door, and wrote on it: This is the helper of Jeremiah.
